prompt: Why can this course not run SwiftData on its recording machine?
hint: Where does SwiftData ship?

choices.text: It needs a paid developer membership
choices.why: SwiftData is free in Xcode; the problem is where it exists.

choices.text: Only Apple's SDKs have it
choices.why: Right: section 05 shows the compiler saying `no such module`.

choices.text: It needs a network connection to Apple's servers
choices.why: It stores on the device; iCloud sync is optional.

choices.text: Linux has no SQLite library
choices.why: Linux has SQLite; the missing piece is the framework itself.

prompt: What does the `@Model` macro add to `SessionRecord` when the app is built?
hint: Two protocols, according to Apple's documentation.

choices.text: `Codable` and `Hashable`
choices.why: Neither is what the documentation names.

choices.text: `PersistentModel` and `Observable`
choices.why: Right: storage, and the observation SwiftUI already watches.

choices.text: `Identifiable` and `Sendable` only
choices.why: The two the documentation leads with are `PersistentModel` and `Observable`.

choices.text: A `save()` method on each record
choices.why: Saving is the context's, not the record's.

prompt: Why does the planner not put `@Model` on lesson 1's `StudySession`?
hint: Two reasons: what `@Model` attaches to, and where the package builds.

choices.text: `@Model` cannot store a `String` date
choices.why: It stores `String`; the records keep the day as text.

choices.text: A struct would sync to iCloud by itself, uninvited
choices.why: Nothing syncs unless the app is configured to.

choices.text: It is a struct, and SwiftData would stop the package building on Linux
choices.why: Right: the values stay portable and testable, and the records are the app's.

choices.text: Apple forbids `@Model` in any Swift package, whatever platforms it lists
choices.why: A package for Apple platforms may use it; this one also builds on Linux.

prompt: Which identifier of a session is sent to the planner's server?
hint: One means something outside this store.

choices.text: `sessionID`, the planner's own id
choices.why: Right: the same id on every platform and every phone.

choices.text: `persistentModelID`, assigned by SwiftData
choices.why: It means nothing outside this store, and differs on a second phone.

choices.text: The row number in the SQLite file
choices.why: Nothing in the planner reads the file's rows.

choices.text: A new UUID made at the moment of sending
choices.why: Then the same session would arrive twice under two ids.

prompt: What does `.modelContainer(for: [CourseRecord.self, SessionRecord.self])` put in the scene's environment?
hint: It is what `@Query` depends on.

choices.text: A list of every record, fetched at launch
choices.why: Fetching is each query's job, when its view appears.

choices.text: A model context for that container
choices.why: Right: `@Query` and `@Environment(\.modelContext)` find it there.

choices.text: An undo manager, switched on
choices.why: Undo is off unless `isUndoEnabled: true` is passed.

choices.text: The path of the store's file
choices.why: The file is the container's business; screens never see it.

prompt: Which store should a preview use, so it never writes sample sessions into the student's plan?
hint: One that lasts only as long as the process.

choices.text: The app's own store, emptied after each preview
choices.why: Emptying it would delete the student's real plan too.

choices.text: A copy of the store, made at launch
choices.why: A copy still lives on disk and drifts from what tests expect.

choices.text: An in-memory one, `inMemory: true`
choices.why: Right: gone when the process ends, for previews and tests.

choices.text: A store in an App Group, shared with the widget
choices.why: That is for sharing real data, the opposite of a preview's need.

prompt: `context.insert(record)` runs and no save has happened yet. Does the new session appear in a `@Query` list?
hint: What does a query read?

choices.text: Yes: queries read the context
choices.why: Right; the save decides when it reaches the disk.

choices.text: No, not until `save()` is called
choices.why: The query sees inserts in the context at once.

choices.text: Only after the app is relaunched
choices.why: Nothing about an insert waits for a relaunch.

choices.text: Only if the view calls `refresh()`
choices.why: A query has no `refresh()`.

prompt: `CourseDetailView` builds its `@Query` in `init`. Why not in the property's own declaration?
hint: The filter depends on the course the view was given.

choices.text: `@Query` cannot take a filter in a declaration, only in an initialiser
choices.why: It can, as long as the filter needs nothing from the view.

choices.text: A wrapper's arguments cannot read the view's other properties
choices.why: Right: the course's id is known only in `init`.

choices.text: A query in `init` runs faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: So the query runs once and never updates
choices.why: It still updates as the context changes.

prompt: What does `#Predicate` produce, that a closure passed to `filter` would not?
hint: It is a macro.

choices.text: Faster Swift code, compiled with optimisations by the macro
choices.why: The point is not speed in Swift but where the filtering happens.

choices.text: A query that runs on a background thread instead of the main one
choices.why: Threads are not what the macro is about.

choices.text: A description of the condition, for a store to evaluate
choices.why: Right, which is why it accepts only what can be described that way.

choices.text: A predicate that also sorts the result
choices.why: Sorting is a separate argument.

prompt: Match what the student does to the code that does it.
hint: The query follows the context.

prompt: On Linux, `import SwiftData` fails with the error `no such ___ 'SwiftData'`.
hint: Read the capture.

prompt: Why do `#Predicate` and `SortDescriptor` run on the course's Linux machine when SwiftData does not?
hint: Which framework are they in?

choices.text: The lab installs a Linux port of SwiftData
choices.why: There is none; the capture shows the import failing.

choices.text: They are Foundation's, not SwiftData's
choices.why: Right: the query is built from them, and they are not SwiftData's.

choices.text: They are compiled to JavaScript on Linux
choices.why: Swift compiles to native code on Linux.

choices.text: Linux evaluates them by asking a Mac on the network
choices.why: Nothing in the lab talks to a Mac.

prompt: The `query` program sorts the mobile course's sessions latest first. Put the ids in the order it printed them.
hint: Dates 27, 22 and 20 October.

prompt: `#Predicate<StudySession> { mondayOf($0.date) == "2026-10-19" }` is refused. What is the fix the section gives?
hint: Compute in ordinary Swift first, then compare stored text.

choices.text: Mark `mondayOf` as `@Predicate` so that the macro accepts the call
choices.why: No such marking exists; a store cannot run your function.

choices.text: Filter every session in Swift after fetching them all
choices.why: It works, and it gives up what the predicate is for.

choices.text: Compare `date` with the week's two days, worked out beforehand
choices.why: Right: two string comparisons, as the third line of the output did.

choices.text: Store each session's Monday as a `Date` instead
choices.why: A `Date` brings back the time-zone problem lesson 1 avoided.

prompt: With the inverse declared, what happens when the code sets `record.course = course`?
hint: The two sides are one fact.

choices.text: The session appears in `course.sessions` with no `append`
choices.why: Right: SwiftData keeps both sides of the relationship in step.

choices.text: Nothing until `course.sessions.append(record)` is also called
choices.why: With an inverse there is one relationship, not two to keep in step.

choices.text: The session is copied into the course, as a value inside it
choices.why: Records are classes, referred to, not copied.

choices.text: The course is saved to disk immediately
choices.why: Saving is the context's, at its own moments.

prompt: Under the default delete rule, a course is deleted. What happens to its sessions?
hint: The default loses nothing.

choices.text: They are deleted with it
choices.why: That is `.cascade`, which the planner chooses.

choices.text: The deletion is refused
choices.why: That is `.deny`.

choices.text: They stay, with `course` set to `nil`
choices.why: Right: `.nullify`, which leaves sessions no screen of the planner shows.

choices.text: They move to the next course in the list
choices.why: No rule reassigns them.

prompt: Match each delete rule to what deleting a course does.
hint: Four rules in Apple's documentation.

pairs.right: its sessions stay, with no course
its sessions still point at it

right_distractors: its sessions are archived for a year

prompt: In a SwiftUI app with `.modelContainer(for:)`, does the main context save by itself?
hint: SwiftData sets one property for the main context.

choices.text: No, every change needs an explicit `save()`
choices.why: Autosave is on for the main context.

choices.text: Yes: `autosaveEnabled` is on there
choices.why: Right; a context you create yourself starts with it off.

choices.text: Only when the app goes to the background
choices.why: It saves after changes and at lifecycle moments, not only then.

choices.text: Only if undo is enabled
choices.why: Undo and autosave are separate settings.

prompt: Why does the planner's save before a sync use `do`/`catch` and not `try?`?
hint: What would the student see if the save failed?

choices.text: `try?` is not allowed on a method that throws
choices.why: It is allowed; it turns the error into nothing.

choices.text: `do`/`catch` makes the save faster
choices.why: Error handling does not change speed.

choices.text: A failed save must reach the screen, not vanish
choices.why: Right: otherwise the student learns next week that nothing was stored.

choices.text: SwiftData retries a save that was caught
choices.why: Nothing retries it by itself; the screen shows the error.

prompt: What does the lesson offer when a student deletes a whole course?
hint: Deleting a course cascades to its sessions.

choices.text: Nothing: deleting is final, by design
choices.why: The lesson argues for Undo.

choices.text: Undo only, with no confirmation
choices.why: That is what a single session gets.

choices.text: A confirmation, and Undo afterwards
choices.why: Right: a bigger loss gets both.

choices.text: A confirmation that has to be typed
choices.why: Nothing that heavy is proposed.

prompt: Version 2 renames `length` to `minutes` without `originalName`. What happens on a phone with version 1's store?
hint: A rename without a name for the old one looks like two changes.

choices.text: The store refuses to open and the app crashes
choices.why: It opens: the danger is that nothing fails.

choices.text: It opens, and every session's minutes are lost
choices.why: Right: one property removed, another added, and no error.

choices.text: SwiftData guesses the rename from the type, `Int`
choices.why: No guess is documented; `originalName` is how it is told.

choices.text: The old column is kept beside the new one
choices.why: The property was removed from the schema.

prompt: Version 2 adds `@Attribute(.unique)` to `sessionID`. Why is its stage `custom` rather than `lightweight`?
hint: What might an old store already contain?

choices.text: Every stage that touches `@Attribute` must be custom, whatever it changes
choices.why: The reason is the data, not the macro.

choices.text: A lightweight stage cannot change a property that holds a `String`
choices.why: The type does not change here.

choices.text: Old duplicates must go first, in `willMigrate`
choices.why: Right: a unique constraint cannot be added over two equal ids.

choices.text: Custom stages run faster on large stores
choices.why: They run code of yours, which is not faster.
